minutes.headline: Sewer Commission discussed raising the late-payment interest rate and demand fee to match nearby towns; no vote was taken.
minutes.summary: The commission approved the prior minutes and heard the first-quarter FY27 demand notice and delinquency report. Most of the meeting was open discussion of raising the late interest rate and the demand fee toward what comparable towns charge. Members leaned toward about 14% interest and a fee between the two figures floated. Nothing was voted; the town manager or staff will ask town counsel about legal limits, and a posted public hearing would be needed. A brief contract update and the meeting calendar followed.

votes.motion: Accept the minutes of the prior meeting (9/8/2026).

budget_items.what_was_said: Staff reported the total owed on first-quarter bills and the share of bills delinquent, with a delinquency rate in a range of roughly 16 to 21 percent depending on measure.
The demand fee is a flat amount that has not changed in about 15 years, charged each quarter a bill is late.
Staff said Lunenburg has the lowest late interest rate among the comparable towns on the spreadsheet and that fee income is needed for the sewer enterprise fund.
Members cited other towns' interest rates and demand fees from the spreadsheet; the speakers corrected each other on which town charged what.

budget_items.topic: Target interest rate and demand fee
budget_items.what_was_said: Members agreed informally on roughly a 14 percent interest rate and a demand fee between the lower and higher figures proposed, pending advice from town counsel.
The current operations contractor remains under contract through November; new bid language has not yet gone out.

Informal consensus on starting figures of about 14% interest and a demand fee between the lower and higher amounts discussed, to be taken to town counsel.

Members reached informal consensus on starting figures of about 14% interest and a demand fee between the two amounts discussed, to be taken to town counsel.

why_it_matters: Sewer users who pay late could face a higher interest rate and a higher quarterly demand fee, and fee income is meant to support the sewer enterprise fund rather than the general tax levy.
Nothing changes until a public hearing is posted and held, so residents will have a chance to comment before any new rate or fee takes effect.
